contract.assumptions: The proposed purge happens after synthesis of the full product. It does not make each ribosomal elongation step wait for a product-state certificate, guarantee chemical identity, or correct ring closure on the ribosome. The donor-empty aliasing failure is recorded separately in N989. Correct transfer onto the next tRNA distinguishes transfer from hydrolysis for the stated two-state comparison; it still does not certify the later intramolecular ring-closing reaction. Chemical-state-negative library selection is therefore a distinct mechanism from product-gated progression at every assembly step.
contract.costs: Credit the existing ribosomal cyclic-backbone chemistry of Lee et al. (2025), established mRNA display linkage from Roberts and Szostak (1997), and the 2026 genetically reprogrammed cyclic glycopeptide mRNA-display result of Johansen-Leete et al. These sources already demonstrate substantial chemistry and genotype-linked selection; this intake did not independently audit their literature. Lee's example is substrate-dependent, and other substrates reportedly cyclize much more efficiently, so those are stronger comparators before adding a filter. Specialized monomers, charged tRNA, flexizyme, GTP-driven translation, puromycin linkage, chemistry-compatible purification, and product recovery remain costs. No integrated synthesis/display/filter machine, measured RNA-compatible capture, or practical advantage is established.
contract.obstruction: Test whether selective aldehyde marking/removal works on the exact uncyclized and cyclized products while intact puromycin-linked mRNA survives; control false tagging at other nucleophiles and identify truncations by product mass. Then test two separately encoded products in one common translation pool with correct mRNA/product identity and quantify the retained library. The source's stated comparison is high-diversity discovery against matched automated synthesis and current mRNA-display/ribosomal methods; no such matched experiment has been run.
contract.provides: Reviewed mechanism proposal for downstream qualification of a finished genotype-linked library, not acquired selective capture/display or step-by-step product gating. RNA compatibility, selective chemistry, distinguishable decoding registers and integrated performance remain open. The 22% substrate example is not the double-ring experiment.
contract.requires: Proposed completed genotype-linked library, credited ribosomal cyclic-backbone synthesis and puromycin display; selective removal must distinguish the exact linear/cyclic products while preserving their attached nucleic acid. This combined selective capture/display interface remains unacquired.

## New constructive attack: Chemical-state-negative proofreading of genotype-linked nonstandard products
Specific chemistry: initial program = distinct mRNA_j; reusable catalyst = shared ribosome and translation proteins; monomers = flexizyme-loaded diester/hydrazinoester tRNAs, already shown to generate programmed hydrazinedione ring. Produce genotype-linked products via established 3'-puromycin mRNA display. After translation, use selective hydrazone ligation (aldehyde) to mark and remove **linear, uncyclized** compounds bearing a free hydrazinyl N; properly cyclized ring has consumed this N and remains unlabelled. The 2025 Lee primary directly showed an uncyclized variant reacts with aromatic aldehyde. Adapt to DNA/RNA-compatible bioconjugation protocols, **but compatibility with intact mRNA fusions and false tagging other functionalities is unacquired**. Immobilized aldehyde scavenger is a speculative engineering realization of this known reaction, NOT an established successful selective purification.
It differs from PnG: destructive failed products can be culled after entire synthesis; intact correctly formed product is not hydrolyzed to edit a carrier. It does not make on-ribosome elongation contingent on cyclization; the potential advance is chemically quality-qualified genotype library generation and selection, rather than perfect autonomous step-level correction. Chemical instruction re-use uses recharged tRNAs / new mRNA molecules, not reusing puromycin-terminated mRNA as catalyst. mRNA-DNA-associated finished molecule is consumed as library object, ribosome is released/reused.

## Quantitative feasibility bound (no assumed rates)
If fraction p=0.22 of genotype-j products have the intended motif and 1-p=0.78 are wrong in the one measured peptide context, and a downstream chemical negative selection retains fraction t of correct molecules and w of wrong, final purity is q=pt/[pt+(1-p)w]. For q≥0.99 require w/t ≤ p(0.01)/(0.99(1-p)) = 0.002849. That is at least 351-fold relative discrimination, regardless of kinetics. If t=0.9, must remove ≥99.744% of incorrect molecules. Two such motifs in the same product independently would produce p²=0.0484 full correctness, and require ~1948-fold selectivity if one final filter. This independence is not measured. Other Lee monomer choices report far better ring fractions, and should be a stronger comparator: use

## Key current primary sources
- K. Lee et al., "Expanded ribosomal synthesis of non-standard cyclic backbones in vitro", *Nat. Commun.* (2025), DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-60126-4, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12120014/. Flexizyme-charged diester initiator and hydrazinoester tRNA, cell-free codon-decoded 5-/6-membered cyclic backbone; tested one 6-membered substrate yields approximately 22% cyclic and 78% linear; products linear react with 4-methylbenzaldehyde to yield hydrazone, which directly established availability of free N on unclosed state. In that particular test peptide was dried and dissolved in aldehyde prior to MALDI—not compatible with intact RNA code as performed. Some tested monomers yielded near 100% motif cyclization, but not uniform across substrates or positions. Two motif chemistry demonstrated, not a new idea here.
- Takayuki Katoh, "EF-P inhibits ribosomal alpha-hydroxy acid incorporation...", *RNA* (2026), DOI 10.1261/rna.081083.126, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13492118/. In cell-free translation, EF-P inhibits alpha-hydroxy on tRNAPro1E2 yet promotes beta/D amino acids. Assigning alpha-hydroxy to EF-P-insensitive AsnE2 and beta/D amino to EF-P-sensitive Pro1E2 allows same-bath multi-chemistry. Phe misincorporation side product observed; full code fidelity NOT established.
- R. Roberts and J. Szostak (1997), *PNAS*, DOI 10.1073/pnas.94.23.12297, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC24913/. mRNA–puromycin linked at 3' enters A site, receives nascent peptide and forms a stable covalent mRNA–product fusion; genotype/product pairing in a shared library is established.
- J. Johansen-Leete et al. (2026), *JACS*, DOI 10.1021/jacs.5c22682, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41779940/. Genetically reprogrammed cyclic glycopeptides were produced and affinity-selected via mRNA display, including bioactive functional molecules; powerful incumbent.
- J. Bath & A. Turberfield, "Mechanism for a molecular assembler ... parallel DNA and a DNA polymerase", *Nanoscale Horizons* (2026), DOI 10.1039/D5NH00505A, https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlehtml/2026/nh/d5nh00505a. Adaptor's 3'-OH released upon putative chain transfer primes Bst strand-displacing DNA polymerase to advance instructions. Primary article explicitly says all subcomponents investigated except the aminoacyl transfer steps: full assembly NOT demonstrated.
- R. Abdul

## Correction from full Lee 2025 double-ring experiment: code address is not freely assignable
Fig. 8 uses two prescribed diester charging addresses: monomer 1 charged to initiator tRNA(fMet)(CAU) decoded at AUG, and monomer 12 charged to tRNA(Pro1E2)(GUC) at a reassigned internal Asp GAC codon, with hydrazine on a separate tRNA(Pro1E2)(ACG) decoded at Arg CGU. Two ring motifs in one ribosomal product were demonstrated. **Mixing two different diesters charged to the same tRNA species or decoded by the same codon does not provide individually selectable instructions**. To realize different chemical commands for two programs in one bath, reassign distinct codons to distinct charged tRNA body/anticodon pairs, or use separated reactors. Moreover, Lee's two-ring Figure 8 controls monomer placement, not arbitrary dynamic program rewrites, proofread ring closure, or genotype-product linkage by mRNA-display puromycin. Lee 2025 22% cyclic is from a particular 6-ring substrate '5', NOT the Figure 8 multiple-ring substrate mixture. Avoid applying the 22% measurement numerically to Fig. 8.

One strong construction is to retain their established AUG + GAC + CGU anticodon assignments for *two chemically different monomer types* in one RNA translation and then add a 3'-puromycin display stage. This implements different placement under codon program but does not yet show per-chain independent late-choice of monomers at the same codon. To achieve that additional operation, a genuinely distinguishable decoding register is needed. A common feed global tRNA charge is not sufficient.

## Exact quantitative library coverage requirement
For a *hypothetical* per-genotype correct ring fraction p and downstream correct-retention t, with N independent successful molecular translation trials per genotype and rare event probability pt, P(at least one right, retained) = 1-(1-pt)^N (fixed N); 95% coverage requires N ≥ ln(0.05)/ln(1-pt). For p=0.22, t=0.9, N≥14 (since 1-.198=.802; ln(.05)/ln(.802)≈13.58). Under Poisson translation count per genotype mean λ instead, coverage is 1-exp(-λpt); λ≥15.13. These are sampling requirements, not data on real mRNA-display throughput or genotype library population distributions. If 22% is due to abortive peptide truncation rather than accessible linear motif, aldehyde capture cannot classify that part; verify target chemical mass.

statement: The source proposes encoding distinct nonstandard peptide products on separate mRNA templates, using established ribosomal elongation and mRNA-display linkage, then applying a downstream chemical-state-negative filter to a completed genotype-linked library. In its example, an uncyclized hydrazinoester product retains an exposed hydrazinyl nitrogen that can react with aldehyde, while the desired cyclic product has consumed that nitrogen. Marking/removing the linear products could qualify library members before functional selection. The source proposes adapting known hydrazone chemistry to intact mRNA fusions; selective capture in an RNA-compatible environment, fusion survival, side-reaction rates, and false tagging have not been demonstrated. The immobilized aldehyde scavenger is speculative.
title: Chemical-state-negative filtering proposes a product-qualified ribosomal display library
